39689874.bottom_line: ESGE's 2025 document sets out what endoscopic sampling can achieve in a bile duct stricture and, for perihilar disease, recommends adding fluoroscopy-guided biopsy to brush cytology and reserving EUS-guided sampling for patients in whom curative resection is not feasible. Seven of its eight recommendations are conditional on low or very low quality evidence, the perihilar recommendation pools two retrospective cohorts totalling 101 patients, and no voting record or agreement threshold is published for any statement. Its scope stops at tissue diagnosis, it offers nothing for the patient with primary sclerosing cholangitis in whom cytology fails, and the restriction it places on EUS in hilar disease is not supported by the seeding data printed in the same section.

The explanations offered for the 25% false-negative rate are inadequate sampling, low specimen tumour cellularity and malignant alterations not covered by the assay
critique: A co-author developed the BiliSeq panel and reported the originating study (Singhi, Gut 2020), and the index test was run in his own institution's molecular pathology laboratory, so this real-world validation is not independent of the test's originators

Specificity and positive predictive value are 100% for cytology and for cytology plus biopsy because the reference standard was assembled by reviewing pathology results, imaging findings and treatments; the pathology index test is therefore part of its own reference standard and cannot generate a false positive

Benign status rests on a mean follow-up of 327 days with a standard deviation of 321, against a stated minimum of 6 months; one of the two BiliSeq false positives was an intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasm with KRAS and GNAS mutations, that is a genuine neoplasm counted as benign

The brush cytology row gives sensitivity 40.7% with an interval (22.4%-61.2%) consistent with a denominator of 27 while every other row uses 28, so the tests compared by McNemar are not computed on identical patients

The management-change endpoint counts test positivity rather than an observed change of decision: it is defined as a malignant stricture with negative pathology in which BiliSeq was positive, and the paper then states that BiliSeq results supported surgical decisions in combination with other diagnostics while chemotherapy regimens followed standard protocols rather than BiliSeq findings alone

Of the 12 patients behind the 75% figure, 2 went to hospice and 4 had pancreatic or distal disease treated by pancreatoduodenectomy; only 2 had a hilar-relevant outcome, one listed for transplantation who died waiting and one liver resection
Stricture location is recorded only as intrahepatic, extrahepatic or both, with no hilar category anywhere in the paper, so the perihilar subgroup cannot be identified at all
No numbered flow of exclusions is given and the exclusion criteria are written as a single disjunction, so the sampling frame behind the 77 patients cannot be audited

BiliSeq was run on bile aspirate or on brush cytology according to the preference of the performing endoscopist, and the split between the two specimen types is never reported, so the index test is two different tests pooled
Cholangioscopy-guided biopsy was excluded by design, yet at this centre cholangioscopy is what follows a non-diagnostic first ERCP, so the comparator is weaker than the local standard pathway

39716538.n: 77 patients with biliary strictures who had brush cytology, transpapillary biopsy and BiliSeq next-generation sequencing at one ERCP at a single US centre between September 2020 and August 2022: 28 malignant and 49 benign strictures, 24 (31.2%) with primary sclerosing cholangitis and 20 with cholangiocarcinoma
39716538.bottom_line: In 77 patients sampled at a single ERCP, adding the BiliSeq panel to cytology and biopsy raised sensitivity for a malignant stricture from 42.9% to 85.7%, which supports running next-generation sequencing on ERCP material when pathology is negative. critique: Industry covered 55% of the conference's costs. The funding statement asserts that no industry representatives sat on any committee, panel or jury, but names no company, discloses no amounts, and the document carries no individual author conflict-of-interest statement at all

Quality appraisal used an in-house four-level scale (high, acceptable, low, unacceptable) rather than a validated instrument, applied by 17 surgical and research fellows described in the Discussion as a group of young academic surgeons, with low-quality studies admitted whenever nothing better existed

The systematic search ended in March 2024 and was then expanded by the panel experts to November 2024, so the most recent evidence entered through unblinded expert selection outside the two-reviewer blinded screening and appraisal process

The transplantation section states in one sentence that the superiority of transplantation over resection is clearly established by a recent 17-centre benchmark study and in the next that the available overall survival data remain imprecise, with one adjusted analysis showing an advantage in the transplant group and another no difference; a benchmark study describes best achievable outcomes and is not a comparative trial

The Mayo criteria are said to have been convincingly validated in a large multicentre cohort of 214; 214 is the number transplanted in that report and not the 287 enrolled, so the validation is quoted on the post-transplant denominator

The living-donor recommendation imports a threshold from other oncological indications, an anticipated post-transplant survival benefit above 50% at five years, and declares it de facto established in perihilar disease by quoting 5-year overall survival of 53%; that figure is the intention-to-treat survival of the whole enrolled multicentre cohort, not a post-transplant or living-donor estimate

The resectability criteria the jury adopted appear only in a supplemental table and figure and are conceded to need validation, while the jury simultaneously declines to endorse any staging system for predicting resectability, so the central operative decision is left to an unvalidated proposal

The drainage-route recommendation names endoscopic drainage as preferred where tumour anatomy allows, records that percutaneous drainage remains what most surveyed centres actually do, and then defers to individual circumstances, so it cannot be acted on in either direction

Panel representation is uneven: 40 of 71 experts (56.3%) are European, 17 (23.9%) North American, 12 (16.9%) Asian and 2 (2.8%) South American with none African, and the audience whose discussion fed the jury was 226 self-selected conference attendees

Adjuvant capecitabine is endorsed although the pooled biliary tract cancer trials the recommendation draws on showed no benefit in the perihilar subgroup, in a document that insists elsewhere that intrahepatic and extrahepatic disease are distinct entities and that those trials are underpowered for perihilar disease

The surveillance protocol of three-monthly CT in the first year then six-monthly for five years with CEA and CA 19-9 is adopted on the stated grounds that it best reflects current standard of care, with no evidence of benefit, no cost consideration and no account of cumulative radiation exposure

40478744.n: 71 international experts in eight panels considering 570 studies published January 2000 to March 2024, with a ten-member jury of hepatologists, non-hepato-pancreato-biliary surgeons, epidemiologists and bioethicists, none directly involved in the care of or research into perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, at a two-day consensus meeting in Milan on 5-6 December 2024 with 226 on-site attendees; there is no patient cohort
40478744.bottom_line: The Milan jury-based consensus is the most comprehensive current statement on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, covering definition, staging, drainage, liver augmentation, the operation, systemic therapy, transplantation and outcome metrics, and it is candid that 84% of its 570 studies are observational and that most surgical recommendations sit at level of evidence 4. Its two central positions are unresolved by its own evidence: the resectability criteria it adopts are expert opinion awaiting validation while it declines to endorse any staging system for predicting resectability, and it extends transplantation to node-negative patients independent of resectability on a benchmark study and mixed retrospective comparisons after TRANSPHIL failed to recruit. Industry covered 55% of the conference's costs, no individual author conflict statement is printed, and no voting record exists for any recommendation.

limitations: Most of the recommendations in the guideline are based on low quality evidence, and the panel calls for high quality prospective studies and randomised trials given the constant technical evolution of therapeutic endoscopy

The quality of evidence for endoscopic against percutaneous preoperative drainage was downgraded to moderate because the risk of inconsistency could not be assessed, the evidence being a single randomised trial
For palliative hilar drainage the quality of evidence was downgraded to very low for high risk of bias in the literature, imprecision and publication bias

The evidence that percutaneous drainage carries greater morbidity than endoscopic drainage comes from trials dedicated to the preoperative setting and not to palliation, which the authors name as the central limitation when applying it to palliative drainage

Prospective extended experience in maximum biliary drainage and prospective evaluation of liver volumetry for palliative hilar obstruction, with survival and access to chemotherapy as the main outcomes, are listed as unmet needs

The number of endoscopic or EUS procedures required to achieve clinical success, and their associated cost and environmental impact, are named as a major gap in the literature when comparing procedures

The meta-analysis favouring percutaneous therapeutic success is limited by the fact that only one of its eleven studies was randomised, that 74% of the lesions were Bismuth III-IV, and that only 30% of the cohort received bilateral drainage
critique: A strong recommendation for endoscopic over percutaneous preoperative drainage in hilar obstruction is issued on a single randomised trial of 54 patients stopped at half its planned accrual, whose own authors call the mortality finding prone to type I error and whose primary endpoint was negative (severe complications 67% against 63%, relative risk 0.94, 0.64-1.40); the evidence is downgraded only to moderate

The guideline's own best comparative data run the other way: the meta-analysis cited in the same section gives percutaneous drainage higher therapeutic success (OR 3.5, 95%CI 2.1-6.0) with 11.5-fold more reintervention after endoscopic drainage (OR 11.5, 3.5-37.7), and the preference for endoscopic drainage is nonetheless stated in that section

The implantation-metastasis meta-analysis is quoted as confirming a higher risk with percutaneous drainage while the printed effect is OR 0.35 (95%CI 0.23 to 0.53), an odds ratio below 1, so the direction of the stated conclusion does not match the reported estimate

Two recommendations in the same subsection point in opposite directions for the same patient: endoscopic drainage is strongly recommended over percutaneous drainage for preoperative drainage in hilar malignant obstruction, and routine preoperative drainage is conditionally recommended against

No voting, agreement threshold or record of dissent appears anywhere; adaptations to recommendations and to their evidence grades were agreed by consensus among involved authors at an on-site meeting during ESGE Days 2025

The liver-volume target is raised from more than 50% to ideally 70% or more on low quality evidence, while the supporting cohorts place it at 50% and at 80% and no meta-analysis or comparative trial has ever tested a percentage threshold; the authors list prospective volumetry as an unmet need in the same document

The preference for EUS-guided drainage over percutaneous drainage in Bismuth III-IV rests on case series of 20, 34, 41 and 88 patients and on one propensity-matched comparison reporting a 58% adverse-event rate in the percutaneous arm, far above the 24% to 35% rates in the document's own other citations

The literature search ran only from 2017 to August 2024 as an update of the 2018 guideline, restricted to English, with further manual searches to 2025 performed by the authors at final editing and therefore outside the systematic process

This reverses the 2018 ESGE position, which allowed percutaneous drainage or combined endoscopic and percutaneous drainage for Bismuth III-IV, without new randomised evidence: the only post-2017 study in the supporting meta-analysis is the same prematurely terminated trial

The palliative hilar recommendation is graded very low quality and still states an order of preference, endoscopic drainage, then endoscopic plus EUS-guided drainage, over primary percutaneous drainage, which is a stronger claim than very low quality evidence supports

Scope is endoscopic only: nothing addresses resectability, the extent of hepatectomy with caudate resection, portal vein embolisation or transplant candidacy, so a surgeon cannot read off when drainage should be deferred or routed to protect a planned operation

Five authors declare consultancy, advisory or lecture relationships with the manufacturers of the stents and delivery systems whose use the recommendations expand, and the document does not record how those interests were managed

The bilateral-stent evidence cuts both ways in the same manner: in the cited randomised trial and in a 236-patient series, technical success was higher with unilateral stenting (98.8% against 82.5%) while clinical success favoured bilateral stenting, and the recommendation follows clinical success

Compare the 2024 Asia-Pacific consensus (PMID 39285860), which on much the same evidence sets the drainage target at more than 50% and favours multiple plastic stents in likely chemotherapy responders; the two documents disagree on route, target and stent choice
No linked editorial or comment was found in PubMed, the guideline having been published online 3 September 2026
42692059.bottom_line: The 2026 ESGE guideline moves endoscopic drainage ahead of percutaneous drainage for hilar malignant obstruction in both the preoperative and the palliative setting, and raises the drainage target to more than 50% and ideally 70% or more of viable non-atrophic liver volume. The preoperative preference is a strong recommendation built on one prematurely terminated 54-patient trial whose primary endpoint was negative, while the same section prints a meta-analysis giving percutaneous drainage higher therapeutic success (OR 3.5, 95%CI 2.1-6.0), and the volume target has never been tested against survival, its supporting cohorts placing it at 50% and at 80%. Nothing in the document addresses resectability, extent of hepatectomy, portal vein embolisation or transplant candidacy, so it cannot tell a surgeon when to defer or redirect drainage.

limitations: The relatively small cohort size may affect the precision of the diagnostic accuracy estimates and limits subgroup analyses, particularly in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis

The follow-up period used to exclude malignancy in patients without histological confirmation was relatively short; although a minimum of 6 months has been applied in previous studies, longer surveillance may be required to detect slowly progressive malignancy, particularly indolent cholangiocarcinoma or PSC-associated cancer, so misclassification of benign cases cannot be excluded and may have influenced the reported performance

Reported diagnostic performance of next-generation sequencing varies widely across cohorts, likely reflecting differences in patient selection, prevalence of malignancy, representation of primary sclerosing cholangitis, sampling and analysis strategies, so independent well-characterised cohorts remain important for validation
Most previous studies of next-generation sequencing in indeterminate biliary strictures have been retrospective or single-centre with relatively small cohorts
No formal limit-of-detection validation study was performed for the assay
The specific molecular alterations detected were not further characterised with respect to their therapeutic actionability
critique: Table 1 reports everything per biopsy rather than per patient, with denominators that change by parameter (47 for sequencing and histopathology, 37 for imaging, 33 for CA 19-9), so the McNemar comparisons are made across different subsets and the number of patients behind the 47 biopsies is never stated

The study was powered to detect a 30 percentage point difference in 32 patients, while the observed difference between histopathology alone (52%) and the combination (78%) is 26 points, and the single reported P value of 0.03 is one McNemar test among the eight comparisons laid out in Table 1 with no adjustment

The panel is not BiliSeq: two in-house gene lists were used, a 21-gene nNGM panel and a 6-gene 'Bili Panel', described only as similar to the approach reported by Singhi, and which samples went through which panel is not stated, so this validates a locally assembled gene set rather than the assay whose figures it is compared against

Variants were called at a 5% allele frequency threshold for non-hotspot regions and as low as 1% for selected hotspots, with no limit-of-detection validation and no list of which variants were treated as hotspots, so the same cohort is read at two different analytical sensitivities

The alternative analysis calling variants of unknown significance pathogenic is printed in parentheses throughout Table 1 with no stated primary analysis rule; it raises sensitivity to 83% while dropping specificity to 71% and positive predictive value to 73%, and the abstract, Key Points and Lay Summary quote only the favourable column

Histopathology is credited with 100% specificity and 100% positive predictive value while benign status was assigned by the absence of histological malignancy together with radiological follow-up, so both histopathology and imaging are tested against reference standards that contain them

The combination rows count a positive result on either test as positive, which cannot lower sensitivity and cannot raise specificity, so reporting that the combination preserved specificity at 96% is arithmetically forced once histopathology has no false positives

CA 19-9 thresholds of 44 U/mL, and above 129 U/mL in primary sclerosing cholangitis, were imported from Singhi rather than derived locally, and applied to a cohort whose PSC proportion is never reported

Not one of the accuracy figures in Table 1 carries a confidence interval, and the report contains no patient flow diagram, no baseline table, no stricture locations, no PSC count and no malignancy prevalence
Nothing distinguishes perihilar from distal or intrahepatic strictures anywhere in the report, so it does not speak to hilar disease specifically

A sensitivity of 65%, or 78% combined with histopathology, still misses roughly a quarter of malignant strictures, and a negative predictive value of 74% to 82% is not high enough to stand down a resection decision on a negative test
The therapeutic-relevance claim lists KRAS, ERBB2, FGFR1, FGFR2 and MAP2K alterations with no counts and no actionability assessment, and names the last gene as MAP2K without its number

Section 3, the Results, did not survive text extraction from the published brief report, so every figure available here comes from the abstract, Table 1 and the Discussion, and the cohort itself cannot be inspected

42698384.n: 47 ERCP-obtained biliary forceps biopsies from patients with biliary strictures of unknown aetiology in routine care at one German centre, with imaging available for 37 and CA 19-9 for 33, against a power calculation of 32 patients assuming a 50% malignancy rate; the Results section is missing from the published text obtained, so the number of patients, the malignancy prevalence and the size of the primary sclerosing cholangitis subgroup could not be read
42698384.bottom_line: This German brief report is real-world confirmation that sequencing cancer-associated genes in ERCP biopsies adds sensitivity to histopathology in an indeterminate stricture: 65% against 52% alone and 78% combined, at specificity around 96%. It is 47 biopsies read at two allele-frequency thresholds with no limit-of-detection validation, no confidence interval on any figure, benign status assigned on 6 months of imaging follow-up, and the Results section missing from the published text obtained, so the cohort itself cannot be inspected. The panels used are locally assembled gene lists rather than BiliSeq, and no stricture is identified as perihilar, so it does not fix the operating characteristics for a hilar stricture.
